purpose: Find the smallest primary-source-grounded mechanisms that can close the current Frankenstein-2.0 WP105 post-dispatch ambiguity/idempotency gap without duplicating already-implemented semantic request hashing and without introducing a second truth store or effect authority.

architecture_delta_fusion.trigger6_reconciliation_rule: Do not duplicate AgentSight E2 or same-snapshot architecture fuser work; move to DISCOVERY_SCOUT.

material_f2_delta_since_reconciliation.finding: The earlier semantic-request-binding gap is no longer the active source gap. Current F2 source now carries immutable EffectRequestIdentity and request_sha256 through intent, canonical authority evidence, PRE/POST correlation and executor evidence. The newest Trigger-4 delta instead freezes a post-process-start timeout mismatch: F2 classifies the executor outcome as unknown, while the exact bound EntityOS EffectGate catches the exception and journals FAILED.

canonical_effect_authority_bound_source.observed_behavior: EffectGate begins a PENDING journal row, calls entityos_bridge.run, and catches any bridge exception as FAILED. EffectJournal has UNKNOWN_AFTER_RESTART recovery for still-PENDING effects, but no distinct post-dispatch UNKNOWN finalization path in the bound source.

research_question: After immutable semantic request hashing is already present, what minimal mechanism should distinguish semantic equality, retry identity, invocation identity and ambiguous post-start outcome so F2 never duplicates a non-idempotent effect and never upgrades uncertainty to a negative world fact?

primary_sources.title: RFC 9110 HTTP Semantics, Section 9.2.2 Idempotent Methods
primary_sources.direct_mechanism: Automatic retry is justified for idempotent semantics after communication failure. A client SHOULD NOT automatically retry a non-idempotent request unless it knows the semantics are idempotent or can detect that the original request was never applied.
primary_sources.f2_relevance: A post-start timeout/transport exception is insufficient evidence that a non-idempotent world effect did not happen. Default action must be UNKNOWN/no automatic replay unless an operation-specific idempotency or verifier contract closes the uncertainty.

primary_sources.title: Python subprocess documentation
primary_sources.direct_mechanism: Popen.wait/communicate can raise TimeoutExpired after process start; timeout is a waiting/termination condition, not an attestation that earlier child side effects did not occur. subprocess.run kills and waits for the child on timeout, but already-performed external effects are outside that cleanup guarantee.
primary_sources.f2_relevance: The current F2 post-start timeout falsifier is correctly conservative at the executor boundary; EntityOS FAILED journal classification cannot be interpreted as certain non-application.

primary_sources.title: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
primary_sources.direct_mechanism: Amazon prefers a unique caller-provided client request identifier instead of inferring retry identity solely from a hash of request parameters. Identical parameters can represent two intentionally separate operations. The service records the token with request parameters; same token with changed intent is a mismatch. Atomic storage of the token and service mutation is required when both belong to one transactional boundary.
primary_sources.f2_relevance: EffectRequestIdentity/request_sha256 is semantic identity, not retry identity. F2 needs a separately scoped stable operation/retry identity if it ever supports safe retry. Existing invocation_id or durable autonomy goal/step identity may be reusable only if their stability/semantics are proven; do not silently redefine them.

primary_sources.title: Ensuring idempotency in Amazon EC2 API requests
primary_sources.direct_mechanism: A repeated request with the same client token and same parameters can succeed without another action; reuse of the same token with changed parameters fails with IdempotentParameterMismatch.
primary_sources.f2_relevance: Supports an explicit tuple of stable retry key plus immutable semantic request digest, with mismatch rejection before dispatch.

primary_sources.title: Stripe API idempotent requests
primary_sources.direct_mechanism: The first executed request result is associated with an idempotency key; later same-key requests return the prior result, and changed parameters are rejected. Results are recorded only once endpoint execution begins; validation/concurrent conflicts are treated separately.
primary_sources.f2_relevance: Useful donor for separating pre-execution validation/conflict from post-start operation identity and for avoiding duplicate execution, but it is not itself evidence that arbitrary subprocess effects are retry-safe.

discovery_findings.claim: request_sha256 must remain semantic identity only. It must not become the retry/idempotency key because two intentional invocations may have identical semantic payloads.
discovery_findings.falsifier: A current F2 contract explicitly proves that identical semantic payloads are forbidden from representing distinct intentional effects and defines request_sha256 as the stable operation identity. No such contract was observed in the current source.

discovery_findings.claim: After executor entry, TimeoutExpired or an analogous transport exception cannot justify automatic replay for a potentially non-idempotent effect unless F2 has an operation-specific idempotency contract or authoritative verifier that proves non-application.
discovery_findings.falsifier: The exact target operation is proven idempotent for the same stable operation key, or an authority-owned verifier deterministically proves the first attempt was not applied.

discovery_findings.claim: The bound EntityOS EffectGate currently maps any bridge exception to journal status FAILED, while current F2 deliberately raises ExecutorOutcomeUnknown for a post-start timeout. This collapses uncertainty at the canonical journal boundary and is the current semantic mismatch to resolve; it does not mean the external effect failed to occur.
discovery_findings.falsifier: A newer admitted EffectGate/EffectJournal source changes the bound behavior or exact runtime evidence proves the relevant exception can only happen before any effect application.

discovery_findings.claim: The minimal donor composition is an F2/EntityOS-native retry envelope, not a new workflow/event database: keep request_sha256 for semantic equality; use a separate stable operation/retry key; bind both to effect/invocation identity and generation; reject same retry key with different request_sha256; prevent second dispatch while outcome is PENDING/DISPATCH_STARTED/UNKNOWN; permit automatic retry only for explicitly idempotent/verifiably-not-applied targets; preserve ambiguous post-start outcomes as UNKNOWN pending authority-owned verification.
discovery_findings.falsifier: A smaller existing canonical primitive already provides equivalent stable retry identity, semantic mismatch rejection and post-start uncertainty handling without semantic overloading.

counterhypotheses.claim: Existing invocation_id is already a stable retry/idempotency key and no new field/contract is necessary.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Trace invocation_id creation across retry/restart/deferred-return paths. It is reusable only if the same logical operation retains the same invocation_id across admissible retries while intentionally repeated identical operations receive distinct IDs.

counterhypotheses.claim: Current durable autonomy goal_id + autonomy_step_id replay fence is sufficient for all effect callers.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Enumerate EffectGate callers. Bound source explicitly excludes non-workspace/direct callers from this autonomy-specific replay fence, so general coverage is not established.

counterhypotheses.claim: Killing a timed-out subprocess proves its effect did not occur.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: A deterministic child can perform a local side effect before sleeping past the timeout; process termination cannot retroactively undo that already-applied effect. Trigger-4 may run this as a bounded falsifier if useful.

counterhypotheses.claim: Importing a full durable workflow/event-sourcing framework is the safest solution.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Compare against a native UnifiedDB/EffectJournal implementation on duplicate-dispatch prevention, semantic mismatch rejection, restart behavior, latency, dependency surface and authority duplication. Current evidence does not justify a second truth/effect substrate.

minimal_handoff_candidate.name: UNKNOWN_SAFE_EFFECT_RETRY_ENVELOPE/v0
invariants: retry_identity + changed semantic_request_digest => reject before dispatch
ambiguous post-start outcome => UNKNOWN until authoritative verification
UNKNOWN => no automatic replay for non-idempotent/unverified operations
idempotent/verifiably-not-applied operations may define an explicit retry policy
all durable evidence remains in canonical UnifiedDB/EffectJournal; no second effect authority
candidate_fields: operation_retry_id (new only if no existing stable identifier proves the required semantics)
invocation_id (existing occurrence/call identity; role must not be silently redefined)
minimal_handoff_candidate.candidate_state_rule: A distinct post-dispatch UNKNOWN semantic state is preferable to overloading FAILED or UNKNOWN_AFTER_RESTART. Trigger6 does not authorize the canonical status change; Trigger4/current authority must integrate and test any schema/API change.

recommended_next_discriminator.task: Inspect exact current F2 invocation/retry/deferred-return IDs and the bound EntityOS journal schema to determine whether an existing stable identity can serve operation_retry_id. Produce a minimal ABI/state-transition patch contract and a deterministic no-real-effect matrix. Include a child-process falsifier that performs a bounded local marker mutation before timing out, proving why post-start timeout must remain UNKNOWN; do not execute or promote it from Trigger6 unless the admitted experimental slot/authority permits.
required_matrix: same retry id + same digest + prior VERIFIED => no second dispatch / prior semantic result
same retry id + different digest => zero dispatch mismatch
same retry id + PENDING or DISPATCH_STARTED => zero concurrent duplicate dispatch
post-start timeout after observable marker => UNKNOWN, not FAILED-as-nonapplication
UNKNOWN + non-idempotent target => no automatic replay
UNKNOWN + authoritative verifier proves not applied => retry may be considered under explicit policy
intentional second identical semantic request + distinct operation id => remains independently executable
